clue.text: Hat she lost in open spaces

indicators.note: letters that are lost have gone astray, so the six letters of the first two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone's hat blows away while they are out on the open moors.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaths are stretches of open, uncultivated land, so they are open spaces.

clue.text: Woman's companion, the Spanish astronomer

parts.note: hers means belonging to a woman
CH is a Companion of Honour, a British order
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A woman's partner, said to be the Spanish stargazer.
explanation.definitionFit: William Herschel was the astronomer who discovered Uranus; his sister Caroline was also one.

clue.text: About to get into pictures, caper around P's domain

indicators.note: the caper word goes around the rest

parts.note: an antic is a caper or prank

indicators.note: the about letter gets into the pictures word

parts.note: art is pictures
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Cavorting about, ready to get into the movies, in the realm of P.
explanation.walkthrough: P is Penguin throughout. 'About' is circa here, not the container signal; 'around' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguins (P) live in the Southern Hemisphere, most famously in the far southern polar region.

clue.text: Cyclist's short impression of a tomboy

parts.note: Sir Chris Hoy is a British Olympic cycling champion

indicators.note: short means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a dent is an impression

explanation.surface: A cyclist's quick sketch of a boisterous girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoyden is a boisterous, high-spirited girl, an old word for a tomboy.

clue.text: Silly smile welcomes Henry King, the beach forager

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the smile word holds the other letters

parts.note: a simper is an affected, silly smile
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A grinning king named Henry wanders along the shore picking things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry King' looks like one person (the Belloc character), but it is H plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimper is someone who catches shrimps, typically netting them along the shore or shallows.

clue.text: The bun Gary had prepared barely survived

indicators.note: prepared as food is made ready, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Gary had made a bun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hanging by a thread is in a precarious state, only just surviving.

clue.text: Mostly drive round fool in a standoff

indicators.note: the shortened drive goes round the fool
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to impel is to drive forward
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Mostly driving round a fool, caught in a deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock in which neither side can make progress, a standoff.

clue.text: Children's P found in bookshop in Guildford

indicators.note: found in means sitting within the following words

explanation.surface: A children's title, P, turned up in a Guildford bookshop.
explanation.walkthrough: Guildford is a town in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Pingu is a claymation penguin from a children's television series.

clue.text: Artist's artistry oddly not an uncommon thing

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: oddly not means the odd-placed letters are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A painter whose skill is, curiously, nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is something seldom found or seen.

clue.text: Stylish ceremony cut short with axes

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
z and y are the names of axes on a graph

explanation.surface: A smart ceremony abruptly curtailed by people wielding axes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritzy is informal for luxurious and fashionable, after the Ritz hotels, so it means stylish.

clue.text: As an example, Magritte comes back with policeman holding a new household tool

indicators.note: the policeman word holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: a cop is a policeman

indicators.note: coming back means the name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Rene Magritte, the Belgian surrealist, supplies an example of the first name Rene

explanation.surface: A surrealist painter returns alongside a policeman who is gripping some new gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As an example' makes Magritte stand for his first name; 'comes back' gives ENER.
explanation.definitionFit: A can-opener is a common kitchen implement for cutting the lids off tins.

clue.text: Limit on red card use irritated P's opponent

parts.note: a cap is a limit

indicators.note: irritated suggests ruffled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cap placed on red cards in a sport annoyed someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Batman, the Caped Crusader, fights the villain the Penguin.

clue.text: Complain about Brussels after very unfair distribution

indicators.note: about means going round, so the complaining word goes round the rest

parts.note: to carp is to complain

indicators.note: after places the Brussels letters behind the letter for very

parts.note: Brussels is home to the EU's institutions, so it stands for EU

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about Brussels after a very unfair share-out of funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A carve-up is an informal term for a dishonest sharing out of spoils between parties.

clue.text: P for one is copper in part

indicators.note: in places the copper symbol within the word for part

parts.note: a bit is a part
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A statement that some element P is partly made of copper.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for Penguin throughout the puzzle; 'in' puts IS and CU between the B and IT of BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Penguin is a well-known British chocolate-coated snack bar, an example of the treat.

clue.text: One going across wasted hours and hours getting food

indicators.note: wasted means lost or squandered, so letters are removed

parts.note: an across entry, here the 1-across solution, the open spaces
a second H, again for hours
a second H, again for hours

explanation.surface: A traveller crossing over, who has squandered hour after hour, finally gets something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One going across' points at 1-across, the first across answer; dropping both its Hs leaves the food word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, as in a place serving good eats.

clue.text: African capital needing North American club host to call round before

indicators.note: needing joins the North American letters on to the rest
the naming word goes round the club host, who is placed after its first letter

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
a DJ, disc jockey, hosts a night at a club

explanation.surface: A city in Africa requiring an American nightclub DJ to drop by beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: N'Djamena is the capital of Chad; 'before' adds nothing to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: N'Djamena is the capital city of Chad, in central Africa.

clue.text: Very strong acid, say, kept in fish tanks

indicators.note: the say letters are kept in the fish tanks

parts.note: aquaria are fish tanks
eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: A powerful acid, for instance, stored in fish tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua regia, nitric and hydrochloric acid mixed, is powerful enough to dissolve gold.

clue.text: Most inhospitable small boat in river

indicators.note: in puts the boat inside the river

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, southern England
an ark is a boat, as Noah's

explanation.surface: A small boat on a river, in the bleakest setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark means bleak and desolate, so the starkest place is the most inhospitable.

clue.text: Complaints of sailor in terrible crash

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the rearranged letters
terrible signals that the letters of crash are mangled

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: The ailments a sailor suffers after a dreadful accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the crash letters into CARHS, and 'in' sets the sailor inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarrh is a medical complaint, an inflammation with excess mucus, so these are ailments.

clue.text: Article about ring following from it

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about or concerning
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a ring and its follow-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereof is formal for of it or from it.

clue.text: P possibly seen in clubs?

definitions.meaning: a penguin ... is formal evening dress, so P (Penguin) could precede this word
clubs is one of the four sets in a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a penguin might be spotted in nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs is one of the four card categories, and a penguin outfit is dinner dress.

clue.text: Officer, also P

parts.note: gen is short for general, an officer
too means also

explanation.surface: An officer, as well as P.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentoo is a species of penguin with a white stripe over its head.

clue.text: P's first to break bone by ancient statue

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the bone

parts.note: the shin is a bone

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the theme abbreviation is taken

parts.note: x means by, as in a measurement of three by two

explanation.surface: A penguin breaks a bone near an old sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Sphinx of Giza is a colossal ancient limestone statue.

clue.text: British Library surrounded by spaces with special signs

indicators.note: the British Library letters are enclosed by the two spaces

parts.note: ems are printing spaces, so two of them give EM EM
L is the abbreviation for library

explanation.surface: The British Library sits among open areas marked with special signage.
explanation.definitionFit: Emblems are symbolic devices or badges, which are signs.

clue.text: Black birds not right for product of P?

indicators.note: not means the right letter is absent

parts.note: rooks are birds

explanation.surface: Black birds lacking a right of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguin is a publishing company, so its output is volumes for reading.

clue.text: A capital back outside P

indicators.note: the turned capital sits outside the word for a, enclosing it
back means the capital's name is written right to left

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
a as in so much a head means per

explanation.surface: A capital city returns, outside some unnamed thing P.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is the 'a' of so much a head, and 'back' gives EMOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor is the largest species of penguin, found in Antarctica.

clue.text: Spooner says which person made hay like Zaphod Beeblebrox

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the opening sounds here are exchanged

parts.note: who asks which person
to ted is to spread hay out to dry, so tedded means made hay

explanation.surface: Asking who had been haymaking, in the manner of a famous fictional galactic president.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of WHO TEDDED gives TWO HEDDED, spelt as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaphod Beeblebrox, in The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, has two heads and three arms.

clue.text: Endless records to play by the fireside

indicators.note: without ends, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: singles are records to put on a turntable

explanation.surface: Playing old discs endlessly while sitting beside the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a domestic fire or fireplace; an inglenook is a chimney corner.

clue.text: Looking for game supported by browser

parts.note: on as in resting on, supported by
Safari is Apple's web browser

explanation.surface: Seeking a game to play, backed up by a web browser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' here is wild animals, not something to play.
explanation.definitionFit: On a safari one is travelling in search of wild animals, which are big game.

clue.text: Books on old soldiers still around

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after

parts.note: ex means former or old
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Literature about veterans that is still in print.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still existing, surviving to the present day.
